# Scam Shield

> Scam Shield is a free, student-built digital-safety website from the ByteBusters Coding Club, Yewa College, Ilaro (Odu'a Investment Foundation), Ogun State, Nigeria. It teaches young people aged 9-17 to recognise online scams, practise on made-up example messages, check a suspicious message (offline red-flag checker plus an optional AI second opinion), report scams and take a quiz.

Key facts:
- Real banks never ask for a PIN, OTP, password or BVN by SMS, call or chat.
- A real prize, job or scholarship never asks you to pay a fee first.
- When unsure: stop, don't share, verify using a contact you already trust, tell a trusted adult.
- All example messages on the site are fictional; links end in ".example".
- Scam Shield is an educational tool, not a commercial fraud-detection system.

## Scam guides
- [Phishing Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/phishing/): A phishing scam is a fake SMS, email or chat message that pretends to come from your bank, school or an app, so you click a link or share your password, PIN or OTP. Real banks in Nigeria never ask for your PIN or OTP by message or phone call.
- [Fake Prizes & Giveaways](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/prize/): A fake prize scam tells you that you have won money, data or a gift in a promo you never entered, then asks you to pay a 'processing fee' or share your details to collect it. A real prize never asks you to pay first.
- [Romance Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/romance/): A romance scam is when someone online pretends to love you or be your close friend, builds trust quickly, and then asks for money, gifts, card photos or private pictures. They usually refuse video calls and always have a sudden emergency.
- [Online Shopping Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/shopping/): An online shopping scam is a fake seller who offers items at a very low price, asks you to pay into a personal account first, and then never delivers. Real sellers usually allow pay-on-delivery, have reviews and give a real address.
- [Tech Support Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/tech/): A tech support scam is a scary pop-up, call or message that says your phone or computer has a virus or an expired licence, then asks you to call a number, install an app or pay to 'fix' it. Real companies do not contact you this way.
- [Investment Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/invest/): An investment scam promises to double your money quickly with 'guaranteed' profit and 'no risk', then asks you to invite friends before you can withdraw. Real investments can lose money, and no honest scheme guarantees fast doubling.
- [Fake Job Offers](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/job/): A fake job offer promises big pay for easy work, skips proper interviews, and asks you to pay a 'registration', 'training' or 'processing' fee before you start. A real employer pays you; they never ask you to pay them to get the job.
- [Impersonation Scams](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/scams/impersonate/): An impersonation scam is when someone pretends to be a friend, family member, teacher or official, often from a new number, and asks for urgent money or secrets. The fix is simple: contact the real person using a number you already have.

## Is this message real? (one page per message, answer in the first sentence)
- [Is the Federal Government grant message on WhatsApp real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/fg-grant-message/): No. Forwarded messages that say the Federal Government is "giving out" a cash grant to everyone, with a link to apply, are scams. Real government programmes are announced on official websites that end in .gov.ng and never ask you to share a message with your contacts.
- [Is the free data giveaway message real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/free-data-giveaway/): Almost never. Messages offering free data from MTN, Airtel, Glo or 9mobile through a link are scams that collect your details or spread the message further. Real data offers appear inside the network's own app or USSD menu.
- [Is the "your account has been blocked" SMS from my bank real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/bank-account-blocked-sms/): Treat it as a scam. A text that says your account or ATM card is blocked and tells you to click a link or send your details is phishing. Banks do not unblock accounts through a link in a message.
- [Is the "update your BVN" message real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/bvn-update-message/): No. Messages asking you to update, link or verify your BVN through a link or a phone call are scams. Your BVN is only handled inside a bank branch or the bank's official channels, and nobody needs you to read it out.
- [Is the "link your NIN or your SIM will be blocked" message real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/nin-linking-message/): Be careful. Messages with a link or a strange number that promise to link your NIN for you are scams. Real NIN-SIM linking is done by you, through your network's official short code, app or shop.
- [How do I know if a credit alert is fake?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/fake-credit-alert/): A fake credit alert is an SMS made to look like a bank alert, sent by a buyer who never paid. The only proof of payment is the balance inside your own banking app or a statement, never the SMS alone.
- [Should I give a POS agent or caller my OTP?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/pos-agent-otp/): No. An OTP is a one-time code that proves it is you. No bank worker, POS agent or "customer care" caller ever needs it. Anyone who asks for your OTP is trying to take money from your account.
- [A friend asked me to send them a WhatsApp code. Is it safe?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/whatsapp-code-request/): No. The 6-digit code WhatsApp sends you is the key to your account. If you send it to anyone, even a "friend", they can take over your WhatsApp and then ask your contacts for money in your name.
- [My friend on WhatsApp urgently needs money. Is it really them?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/whatsapp-friend-needs-money/): Check before you send anything. Hacked or copied WhatsApp accounts are used to ask friends and family for "urgent" money. Call the person on their normal phone line and hear their voice first.
- [Can someone upgrade my JAMB score for a fee?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/jamb-upgrade-score/): No. Nobody can upgrade a JAMB score. People who offer "score upgrading" take your money and disappear, and trying it can also get a candidate into serious trouble.
- [Are WAEC or NECO "expo" and "runs" real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/waec-expo-runs/): They are scams and they are cheating. Sellers of leaked "expo" answers take payment and send fake or wrong answers, and candidates who use them risk cancelled results.
- [Do real scholarships ask for a processing fee?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/scholarship-processing-fee/): No. A real scholarship does not ask a student to pay a "processing", "form" or "clearance" fee to receive the award. A scholarship that asks for money first is a scam.
- [Is a job that asks for a registration fee real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/job-offer-registration-fee/): No. Real employers do not ask job seekers to pay for forms, training, uniforms or an "ID card" before starting work. Paying first is the clearest sign of a fake job.
- [Are "earn daily from your phone" typing or liking jobs real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/work-from-home-typing-job/): Mostly not. Offers that pay you to like videos, type or rate products often pay a little first, then ask you to "deposit" money to unlock bigger tasks. That deposit is the scam.
- [Can an investment double my money in a week?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/investment-doubling-money/): No honest investment can promise to double money in days. Schemes that do are usually Ponzi schemes: early people are paid with later people's money until it collapses and most lose everything.
- [Is the crypto or forex "account manager" on Instagram real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/crypto-trader-on-instagram/): Very unlikely. Strangers who offer to trade for you and show screenshots of profit are running a common scam: you send money, see fake "growth", then must pay more fees to withdraw.
- [Is a loan that asks for an upfront fee real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/loan-app-upfront-fee/): No. A lender that asks you to pay an "insurance", "processing" or "activation" fee before releasing a loan is a scam. Real lenders take their charges from the loan, not before it.
- [Is the "your package is waiting, pay delivery fee" message real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/delivery-fee-package/): If you did not order anything, it is a scam. Fake delivery messages ask for a small fee or your card details to "release" a parcel that does not exist.
- [How do I know if an Instagram or WhatsApp vendor is real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/instagram-vendor-pay-first/): You cannot be sure from the page alone. Fake vendors use stolen photos, very low prices and "payment before delivery only". The safer choices are pay-on-delivery, a shop with a physical address, or a platform that holds the money until you receive the item.
- [Are "Customs auction" cars and rice on Facebook real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/customs-auction-cars/): No. Pages selling cheap "Customs auction" cars, rice or phones and asking for a deposit are scams. The Nigeria Customs Service does not sell goods through Facebook pages or private phone numbers.
- [I got a message that I won a promo I never entered. Is it real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/you-won-a-promo/): No. You cannot win a promo you never entered. The message is bait to get a "claim fee" or your bank details.
- [Is the celebrity or influencer giveaway real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/celebrity-giveaway/): Usually not. Scammers copy the name and photo of a celebrity, then message "winners" asking for a fee, card details or a code. A real giveaway comes from the verified account and never asks winners to pay.
- [My online friend says a gift is stuck at customs. Is it real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/romance-gift-at-customs/): No. The "gift stuck at customs" is one of the oldest romance scams. A second person pretending to be a customs or courier officer then asks you to pay to release a parcel that never existed.
- [Someone is threatening to share my private pictures. What do I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/sextortion-threat/): Do not pay and do not send more. This is called sextortion and it is a crime against you; it is not your fault. Stop replying, keep the evidence, block and report the account, and tell a trusted adult today.
- [A pop-up says my phone has a virus and I should call a number. Is it real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/tech-support-popup/): No. Websites cannot scan your phone. Pop-ups that say you have a virus and tell you to call a number or install an app are scams to take over your device or charge you.
- [Someone asked me to install an app so they can "help". Should I?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/remote-access-app/): No. Apps that share your screen or give remote control let a stranger see your codes and open your banking app. Real customer care does not ask you to install them.
- [Someone called claiming to be from my network and asked for a code. Is it real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/sim-swap-call/): Treat it as a scam. Callers who ask for a code, your NIN or details "to upgrade your SIM" may be trying a SIM swap, which moves your phone number to their SIM so they receive your bank codes.
- [Someone says they sent me money by mistake and wants a refund. What do I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/wrong-transfer-refund/): Do not send money back yourself. This is often a trick using a fake alert, or money from another victim. Tell the person to report to their bank, and let your own bank reverse it if it is real.
- [Someone wants to pay me to use my bank account. Is that okay?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/account-for-rent/): No. Letting someone receive money through your account makes you a "money mule". The money is usually stolen, and the account holder is the one the bank and police look for.
- [Is the house agent asking for a fee before inspection real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/house-agent-inspection-fee/): Be careful. Fake agents advertise a cheap room or flat with stolen photos, then collect "inspection" or "form" fees from many people. Never pay rent before seeing the place and confirming the owner.
- [Can someone change my NYSC posting or school admission for money?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/nysc-posting-change/): No. People who claim to "work" a posting, admission or result for a fee are scammers. These things are handled only through the official portal of the body in charge.
- [Is the message saying I have admission and should pay an acceptance fee real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/admission-list-fee/): Check before paying. Scammers send fake admission messages and collect "acceptance fees" into personal accounts. Real admission status is seen on the official admission portal, and fees are paid through the school's official channel.
- [How do I know if a donation or charity appeal is real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/fake-charity-donation/): Check who is asking. Fake appeals use sad photos, a personal bank account and pressure to give now. A real charity has a registered name, an official account in that name and a way to contact it.
- [A "pastor" or "alhaji" I do not know asked for money for prayers. Is it real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/prophet-or-pastor-request/): Treat it as a scam. Strangers who call or message with a "vision" about you and ask for money, airtime or "seed" are using fear and faith as pressure.
- [Are Telegram "airdrop" and tap-to-earn withdrawal fees real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/telegram-airdrop/): Be careful. Many groups promise coins, then ask for a "gas fee" or your wallet's secret phrase to withdraw. Anyone who gets your secret phrase can empty the wallet.
- [Are "fixed match" and sure-odds sellers real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/sports-betting-fixed-match/): No. Nobody selling "fixed matches" knows the result. They send different predictions to different people so some win by chance, then use those winners as "proof".
- [Is the "buy our starter package and bring 3 people" business real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/business-package-recruiting/): Check carefully. Some offers sell a "business package" that only makes money when you recruit other people. If the income comes from recruiting, not from customers, it is a pyramid scheme.
- [Is the email saying my password has expired real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/email-password-expired/): Usually not. Emails that say your password or mailbox will expire and give a link to "keep the same password" lead to a fake login page that steals it.
- [Is it safe to scan a QR code someone sends me to "receive" money?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/qr-code-payment/): No. You never need to scan a code or enter your PIN to receive money. Scanning a stranger's QR code or approving a request usually sends money out of your account.
- [Are free game coin, diamonds or UC generators real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/game-currency-generator/): No. "Generators" for free game currency do not work. They exist to steal your game account, show endless adverts or install harmful apps.
- [Can a "hacker" on social media recover my account for a fee?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/hacked-account-recovery-agent/): No. People who advertise account recovery in comments and DMs are scammers who take your money and sometimes the account too. Recovery is done only through the app's own help page.
- [Is the travel agent promising a guaranteed visa or job abroad real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/visa-and-travel-agent/): Be very careful. Nobody can guarantee a visa, and offers of easy jobs abroad for an upfront fee are a common scam that can also lead to trafficking. Visas are decided only by embassies.
- [Is the message offering cheap prepaid meter tokens or a free meter real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/electricity-meter-token/): Treat it as a scam. Offers of half-price electricity tokens, "meter bypass" or a free meter for a registration fee from private numbers are tricks to take money or account details.
- [Is the "answer a short survey and win a reward" link real?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/survey-reward-link/): Usually not. Fake surveys copy the logo of a known shop or bank, ask a few easy questions, then tell you to share the link and enter personal details to "claim".
- [Can an agent pay my school fees at a discount?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/is-it-real/school-fees-discount-agent/): No. "Agents" who promise to pay school or exam fees for less use stolen cards or simply keep the money. The school later reverses the payment and the student still owes.

## What to do after a scam
- [I shared my OTP. What should I do now?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-shared-my-otp/): Act quickly. An OTP can approve a payment or a login, so tell a trusted adult now and contact the bank through its official app or the number on the back of the card.
- [I clicked a scam link. What should I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-clicked-a-scam-link/): Clicking alone is usually not the end of the world. The danger is what you typed or installed after. Close the page, then follow these steps.
- [I sent money to a scammer. Can I get it back?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-sent-money-to-a-scammer/): Sometimes, if you act fast. Banks can try to stop or trace a transfer when it is reported quickly, but there is no guarantee. Report it today.
- [My WhatsApp was hacked. How do I get it back?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/my-whatsapp-was-hacked/): Reinstall WhatsApp and register your own number again. The new code sent by SMS logs the hacker out. Then turn on two-step verification.
- [My Facebook or Instagram was hacked. What do I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/my-facebook-or-instagram-was-hacked/): Use the app's own "hacked account" recovery, not a stranger who offers help. Then change your password and turn on two-step verification.
- [Someone made a fake account with my name and photos. What do I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/someone-is-using-my-photos/): Report the fake profile inside the app as "pretending to be me". Ask friends to report it too, and warn your contacts.
- [I gave someone my BVN or NIN. Is that dangerous?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-gave-out-my-bvn-or-nin/): On its own a BVN or NIN cannot move money, but it helps a scammer pretend to be you. Stay alert and never give the codes that follow.
- [I installed an app a stranger told me to install. What now?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-installed-a-strange-app/): Remove it now and assume the stranger may have seen your screen. Then secure your accounts from a different, safe device if possible.
- [I am being blackmailed online. What should I do?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/i-am-being-blackmailed-online/): Do not pay, do not send more, and do not face it alone. It is a crime against you and it is not your fault. Tell a trusted adult today.
- [My parent or grandparent was scammed. How can I help?](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/help/my-parent-or-grandparent-was-scammed/): Be kind first, then help them report quickly. Scams work on clever people every day, and shame makes people hide it and lose more.

## Words to know
- [OTP](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/otp/): An OTP (one-time password) is a short code sent to your phone to prove it is really you approving a login or payment.
- [BVN](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/bvn/): A BVN (Bank Verification Number) is an 11-digit number that identifies one person across all Nigerian banks.
- [NIN](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/nin/): A NIN (National Identification Number) is the 11-digit number that identifies you in Nigeria's national identity database.
- [phishing](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/phishing/): Phishing is when a scammer pretends to be a trusted company in a message, so you click a link and type your password, PIN or OTP on a fake page.
- [smishing](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/smishing/): Smishing is phishing by SMS: a text message that pretends to be your bank, network or a delivery company.
- [vishing](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/vishing/): Vishing is phishing by voice call: a caller pretends to be bank or network staff to get your codes.
- [SIM swap](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/sim-swap/): A SIM swap is when a scammer tricks a network into moving your phone number to their SIM card, so they receive your calls and bank codes.
- [fake alert](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/fake-alert/): A fake alert is a false bank credit message sent by a buyer to make a seller believe they have been paid.
- [Ponzi scheme](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/ponzi-scheme/): A Ponzi scheme is a fake investment that pays early members with money from new members, not from real profit.
- [pyramid scheme](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/pyramid-scheme/): A pyramid scheme is a "business" where you earn mainly by recruiting other people who pay to join.
- [money mule](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/money-mule/): A money mule is a person who lets criminals move stolen money through their bank account, often for a small payment.
- [sextortion](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/sextortion/): Sextortion is blackmail where someone threatens to share private pictures or videos unless you pay or send more.
- [two-step verification](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/two-step-verification/): Two-step verification (2FA) adds a second check, such as a PIN or code, when someone logs in to your account.
- [impersonation](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/impersonation/): Impersonation is when a scammer pretends to be a person or organisation you trust, such as a friend, teacher, bank or government office.
- [social engineering](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/social-engineering/): Social engineering means tricking a person, not a computer: using fear, hurry, kindness or greed to make someone give up money or secrets.
- [advance-fee fraud (419)](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/advance-fee-fraud/): Advance-fee fraud is any scam where you are asked to pay a small fee first to receive something bigger that never comes.
- [romance scam](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/romance-scam/): A romance scam is when someone fakes love or close friendship online to get money, gifts or private pictures.
- [spoofing](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/spoofing/): Spoofing is making a call, text, email or website look as if it comes from someone else.
- [malware](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/malware/): Malware is a harmful app or file that can spy on your phone, steal passwords or show endless adverts.
- [secret phrase (seed phrase)](https://scam-shield-blond.vercel.app/meaning/secret-phrase/): A secret phrase is the list of 12 or 24 words that controls a crypto wallet.
